citation: StataCorp, Stata Base Reference Manual, [R] ologit, Example 1, p. 4 (https://www.stata.com/manuals/rologit.pdf; release 19). The command is `ologit rep77 foreign` and the page prints `Log likelihood = -85.908161`, `Number of obs = 66`, a coefficient on foreign of 1.455878, and the four cut points /cut1 -2.765562, /cut2 -.9963603, /cut3 .9426153 and /cut4 3.123351. The data are the whole cross-tabulation `tabulate rep77 foreign` on the same page: 2/1, 10/1, 20/7, 13/7 and 0/5 domestic against foreign over the five repair records, 66 cars in all.
notes:
WHY THIS SOURCE AND NOT THE METHOD'S OWN. Card #523 cites McCullagh (1980), doi:10.1111/j.2517-6161.1980.tb01109.x, and that paper is where the proportional-odds model and its worked two-sample example live: Table 1 on p. 111 prints the whole 2 x 3 tonsil-size table of 1398 children, and pp. 112-113 print the fit as `Delta-hat = 0.603 +/- 0.225; theta-hat_1 = -0.810 +/- 0.116; theta-hat_2 = 1.061 +/- 0.118` with `G^2 = 0.302 on one degree of freedom`. Every one of those four numbers is printed to THREE DECIMALS, and three decimals is the whole obstacle. MEASURED on that table in this worktree's environment, with the body's own fit: Delta-hat 0.6026415259338052 against 0.603 is 5.9448e-04 relative, theta_1 -0.809828952110833 against -0.810 is 2.1117e-04, theta_2 1.0613983374271192 against 1.061 is 3.7544e-04, and the residual deviance 0.3021876724632646 against 0.302 is 6.2143e-04. All four round to the printed figure exactly, so the estimator reproduces the paper -- and all four sit OUTSIDE `estimate-1e-4`, which is the class an optimiser-driven estimate belongs to. That is arithmetic rather than a measurement that could improve: half a unit in the third decimal of 0.603 is 8.3e-04 of it, so no fit however converged can agree with the printed number to 1e-04. The next class up, `pvalue-1e-3`, would admit all four and its perturbation control would still bite -- but it is documented `for: a p-value, compared near zero where the absolute floor dominates`, and a coefficient is not a p-value; naming it here would describe neither the number nor the reason. So McCullagh's four figures are not claimed HERE. They are asserted at the precision the page actually carries, by `round(x, 3)`, in tests/wrappers/c16_limited_dependent/test_ordered_choice.py, where a three-decimal claim can be written as a three-decimal claim.

WHAT THIS PAGE PUBLISHES INSTEAD. Seven significant digits, on a dataset it prints in full. The cross-tabulation IS the data for `ologit rep77 foreign`: five ordered records by two origins, 66 cars, no other variable in the model, so the estimation sample is reconstructible from the page with nothing left to guess. MEASURED against it: the coefficient agrees at 1.4704e-07, the four cut points at 1.7647e-06, 9.2529e-07, 2.1959e-06 and 1.6389e-07, the log-likelihood at 5.0791e-09 and the observation count exactly. The worst of those is 2.1959e-06, forty-five times inside the class this case names.

WHY estimate-1e-4 AND NOT statistic-1e-6. Every number here comes out of a quasi-Newton iteration rather than a closed form, which is what the class is for, and the sibling count-model case says the same of its own log-likelihood. The worst agreement measured above would in fact fit inside `statistic-1e-6` today, and that is exactly why it is refused: it would pin two different optimisers' stopping points against each other, and neither Stata's nor statsmodels' is a closed form anybody can appeal to. The class BITES on this payload -- ten times its rtol moves 1.455878 to 1.457334, -0.9963603 to -0.9973567, -85.908161 to -85.994069 and 66 to 66.066, and the comparison refuses every one of them.

WHAT MOVES WHEN THE DATASET MOVES. `stata_r_ologit_1977_foreign` is a column of 0 and 1, so the harness perturbs it by NEGATION: domestic and foreign swap, the coefficient becomes -1.455878 and all four cut points shift, so every claimed field moves and the comparison refuses the moved payload. The repair record is perturbed by adding one to each code, which is a relabelling of an ordinal scale and leaves the fit untouched -- that is a property of the method rather than a hole in the control, and the manual's own technical note on this very example says so: `replace rep77=10 if rep77==5 ... we would still obtain the same results`.

NO STANDARD ERROR IS CLAIMED, AND THE REASON IS NOT PRECISION EITHER. The page prints one for the coefficient and one for each cut point, and MEASURED, the first two agree with what this body could report -- 0.5308950509903411 against .5308951 is 9.2315e-08, and the first cut point's 0.5988208369919852 against .5988208 is 6.1775e-08. The other three do NOT, and the reason is the same representation trap this method's card warns about: statsmodels stores the last J-2 threshold parameters as LOG INCREMENTS between cut points, and `bse` reports the standard errors of those, not of the cut points. Against the page's /cut2, /cut3 and /cut4 they are 4.3718e-02, 4.5772e-01 and 6.0102e-01 away. A payload that reported them beside the transformed cut points would be pairing an estimate with another parameterisation's uncertainty, so `coeftable` carries the covariates alone and no threshold inference at all.

WHAT ELSE IS UNCHECKED AND WHY. `marginal_effects` is this engine's own arithmetic from the model's definition, and no ordered-model source found prints one; it is checked instead against a central finite difference of the fitted probabilities, in the module's own tests. The measured agreement is stated THERE and not here, because three different figures for it were once in circulation at once and one copy is what stops that. `link` echoes the argument. `outcome` and `design` are the sample this fit was estimated over, published so that ld_proportional_odds_test -- whose only argument is a handle to this node's return -- can re-fit the binary regressions its test compares; putting the FITTED OBJECT there instead is closed, because to_mcp renders a foreign object as a serialisation stub and tests/controls/double_run.py refuses such a payload outright.

THE SECOND NODE OF THIS CARD HAS NO CASE HERE, AND THAT IS A FINDING RATHER THAN AN OMISSION. Brant (1990), doi:10.2307/2532457, prints its own statistics on 83 donated livers -- omnibus X^2 = 11.2 on 6 degrees of freedom -- and never prints the 83 x 7 design they were computed from, so nothing can be rebuilt to compare against. McCullagh prints his data and no Brant statistic. This dataset publishes neither: MEASURED, its fourth dichotomy 1{rep77 > 4} is separated -- no domestic car has an Excellent record -- so the fourth binary logit has no maximum-likelihood estimate and ld_proportional_odds_test REFUSES this fit rather than reporting a number for it. That node is reached instead by the invocation payload tests/payloads/c16_limited_dependent/ordered_choice/proportional_odds_on_the_tonsil_table.json, which runs it over McCullagh's Table 1 and claims nothing about the result.
